outline.chapter_title: From LSTMs to xLSTM: The Landscape of Sequence Modeling
outline.description: Introduce the motivation and context for xLSTM by reviewing the evolution of sequence models, the LSTM’s core ideas and successes, and the rise of Transformers. Frame the central question of the paper: how far can a modernized, scaled LSTM go in language modeling?
subtopics: Sequence modeling overview: RNNs, LSTMs, State Space Models, Transformers
Vanishing gradients and the constant error carousel
LSTM gates and the cell/hidden state update
Historical successes of LSTMs in language and control tasks
Transformers and self-attention scalability
Motivation to revisit LSTMs at modern LLM scale

outline.description: Detail the three main limitations that motivated xLSTM: difficulty revising stored content, limited storage capacity due to scalar memories, and lack of parallelizability due to memory mixing.
subtopics: Inability to revise storage decisions (Nearest Neighbor Search example)
Limited storage capacity and rare token prediction
Sequential dependency from memory mixing (hidden-to-hidden connections)
How these limits favored attention-based Transformers
Design desiderata for a next-generation LSTM

outline.chapter_title: xLSTM at a Glance: Goals, Components, and Architecture
outline.description: Present the high-level design of xLSTM: introducing exponential gating and new memory structures, and integrating them into residual architectures compatible with modern LLM tooling.
subtopics: Core contributions: exponential gating and modified memory
Two xLSTM variants: sLSTM (scalar memory) and mLSTM (matrix memory)
Heads and cells: memory mixing within sLSTM heads; equivalence of heads and cells in mLSTM
xLSTM blocks and residual stacking into full architectures
Notation xLSTM[a:b] for block ratios (mLSTM:sLSTM)
Intended benefits: revisability, capacity, and efficiency

outline.description: Explain the new exponential gates and the normalization/stabilization mechanisms that make them practical and numerically safe, enabling dynamic revision of memory.
subtopics: Exponential input and forget gates: definitions and intuition
Normalizer state (n_t): tracking effective gate strengths
Stabilizer state (m_t): log-domain max trick to prevent overflow
Stabilized gates (i'_t, f'_t) and invariance of outputs/gradients
Initialization and numerical considerations for robust training
Why exponential gating enables revisable storage

outline.chapter_title: sLSTM: Scalar Memory with Exponential Gating and Memory Mixing
outline.description: Detail the sLSTM cell, which retains scalar memories but augments them with exponential gating, a normalizer, and new memory mixing capabilities via multi-cell and multi-head designs.
subtopics: sLSTM forward pass: cell, normalizer, hidden state, and gates
Forget gate choices: sigmoid vs exponential
Multiple cells and recurrent mixing matrices
Multi-head sLSTM: mixing within heads, not across heads
New memory mixing behavior induced by exponential gates
Parallelization limits and practical CUDA implementation notes
When to use sLSTM blocks in practice

outline.chapter_title: mLSTM: Matrix Memory with Covariance Updates
outline.description: Describe the mLSTM’s matrix memory and outer-product updates, relating it to associative memories and fast weights. Show how gating, normalization, and parallelization are handled.
subtopics: Matrix memory C_t and covariance update rule
Key, value, and query projections (with scaling for keys)
Normalizer vector and denominator stabilization (max of absolute dot and threshold)
Gating roles: input as learning rate, forget as decay, output as retrieval scaling
Connections to Bidirectional Associative Memories and fast weight programmers
Gate stabilization via m_t as in sLSTM
Parallel reformulation (scan) and absence of memory mixing
Capacity–compute trade-offs and practical dimensions

outline.description: Explain how sLSTM and mLSTM are embedded into residual blocks and stacked to form full xLSTM architectures, leveraging pre-LayerNorm backbones and dimension expansion strategies.
subtopics: Pre-LayerNorm residual backbone (pre-LN) and why it’s used
Post up-projection blocks for sLSTM (Transformer-like MLP positioning)
Pre up-projection blocks for mLSTM (SSM-like high-dimensional summarization)
Cover’s Theorem motivation for up-projection
Stacking strategy and block ratio selection (xLSTM[a:b])
Embedding layers, normalization, and output heads
Auto-regressive training objective and teacher forcing

outline.chapter_title: Computation and Memory: Complexity, Parallelism, and Throughput
outline.description: Analyze xLSTM’s computational profile: linear time and constant memory in sequence length, GPU friendliness, and practical performance compared to Transformers and other RNN/SSM models.
subtopics: Time and memory complexity vs sequence length
Comparison to attention (quadratic in context length) and KV caches
Matrix memory compute patterns (d by d) and parallelization
sLSTM vs mLSTM runtime and batching characteristics
Length extrapolation and large-batch decoding advantages
Implementation pathways toward FlashAttention-like kernels

outline.description: Situate xLSTM within the broader literature on attention, linear attention, SSMs, and modern RNNs, emphasizing the common theme of gating and the distinct role of memory mixing.
subtopics: Linear attention approaches: Synthesizer, Linformer, Performer, Hyena, GLA
State Space Models: S4, DSS, S5, H3, Mamba, BiGS
RNN alternatives: LRUs, HGRN/HGRN2, RWKV
Gating as a unifying principle across architectures
Covariance-based updates in RetNet, Linear Transformer, RWKV, HGRN2
Distinctive feature of xLSTM: memory mixing enables state tracking and expressivity

outline.description: Present the datasets, model scales, training setups, and evaluation tasks used to assess xLSTM, including synthetic tasks, long-context benchmarks, and large-scale language modeling.
subtopics: Datasets: SlimPajama 15B and 300B tokens
Model sizes (125M to 1.3B) and block configurations
Training precision and implementation details
Synthetic tasks: formal languages and multi-query associative recall
Long Range Arena for long-context evaluation
Validation perplexity, downstream reasoning tasks (e.g., LMEval), PALOMA
Scaling law analysis: methodology and metrics

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Results: Capabilities, Comparisons, and Scaling
outline.description: Summarize the findings: xLSTM’s state-tracking on formal languages, memory capacity on associative recall, strong long-context handling, superior perplexities, robust scaling, and practical speed.
subtopics: Formal language results: parity and other state-tracking tasks
Associative recall: memory capacity across many key–value pairs
Long Range Arena: handling long sequences
15B-token comparisons: xLSTM vs Transformers, SSMs, and RNNs
Ablation studies: residual backbones, exponential gating, matrix memory, gate inputs
300B-token results: length extrapolation to 16k and validation perplexities
Downstream tasks: broad wins with some ARC exceptions
PALOMA: domain-wise perplexity gains across 571 text domains
Scaling laws: favorable offsets indicating continued gains at larger scales
Inference speed and throughput vs Llama, Mamba, and RWKV

outline.chapter_title: Implementing and Training xLSTM in Practice
outline.description: Provide actionable guidance for building and stabilizing xLSTM models, choosing block ratios, tuning gates, and achieving efficient training and inference.
subtopics: Gate parameterization, biases, and activation choice for forget gates
Stabilization hyperparameters: denominator threshold and log-max trick
Initialization strategies for gates and memory states
Choosing block ratios: xLSTM[1:0] vs xLSTM[7:1] and task fit
Dimensionality, number of heads, and number of cells
Mixed-precision training and compilation considerations
Batching strategies, prefill handling, and decoding throughput
Debugging overflow, underflow, and training instability

outline.chapter_title: Theory and Intuition: Why xLSTM Works
outline.description: Develop a conceptual understanding of xLSTM’s mechanisms: how exponential gates enable revisable storage, how covariance-based memories store associations, and why up-projection helps.
subtopics: Revisable storage via exponential gates and running normalizers
Normalizer as an implicit normalization akin to attention’s denominator
Memory capacity and separability in covariance-based fast weights
Expressivity and state tracking: RNNs vs Transformers/SSMs
Limits of pairwise interactions vs quadratic attention
Cover’s Theorem and the role of up-projection in separating contexts

outline.description: Discuss current bottlenecks and risks, including non-parallelizable components, kernel efficiency, compute costs, and sensitivity to hyperparameters, and outline promising research directions.
subtopics: Non-parallelizable sLSTM and current kernel speed gaps
Unoptimized mLSTM kernels and opportunities for acceleration
Compute cost of d-by-d memory updates in mLSTM
Forget-gate initialization sensitivity and training stability
Potential memory overload at very long contexts and mitigation
Need for broader hyperparameter and architecture search
Future directions: improved kernels, adaptive memory, hybrid models, new domains

outline.description: Recap the xLSTM approach and its empirical standing relative to Transformers and SSMs, highlight when to choose sLSTM vs mLSTM, and provide resources for further exploration.
subtopics: Key takeaways on performance, scalability, and efficiency
Guidance on selecting sLSTM vs mLSTM for tasks
Potential impact areas: reinforcement learning, time series, physical systems
Open-source code and reproducibility (GitHub link)
Suggested readings to deepen understanding
